newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodian co-defence minister cancels return.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian co-defence minister cancels return.

text.p: Tea Chamrath, the Cambodian co-defence minister aligned with ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranarridh, has cancelled plans to return to Phnom Penh due to fears for his safety, security sources said on Wednesday.
The minister, who has been stranded in Thailand since last week due to fighting in the Cambodian capital, had earlier planned to fly back to Phnom Penh by Monday, his aide told Reuters.
He had planned to try to help ease the confrontation between forces loyal to Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and those of powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, Ranariddh's bitter rival.
"He has cancelled his plan to return," the aide said, declining to elaborate.

Reports from Phnom Penh have said that Ranariddh's loyalists were in hiding, fearing arrest by Hun Sen's forces which on Tuesday arrested a senior pro-Ranariddh official, interior minister Ho Sok. He was later shot dead.

The two premiers formed a tense coalition government following U.N.-run elections won by FUNCINPEC in 1993. Months of escalating tension between the two culminated in outright fighting in Phnom Penh at the weekend in which Hun Sen's forces seized control of the capital.
